metadata.title: Unpacking equity. Educational equity in secondary analyses of international large-scale assessments: A systematic review

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study is an interpretive systematic review of secondary analyses using ILSA data, not an analysis of ILSA microdata. Therefore, there is no student-level sampling frame, no replicate-weight scheme, and no weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT, TOTWGT) to apply. The review’s “sample” is the set of included peer-reviewed articles (25 included after screening), selected via database searches and eligibility criteria rather than via ILSA survey sampling. Any weighting considerations relevant to the primary studies are outside the scope of this review and are not operationalized here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this paper does not conduct an empirical analysis of ILSA achievement outcomes; it synthesizes how equity is conceptualized and operationalized across included studies. Missing-data handling is not reported because the review does not fit statistical models to individual student records; instead, it applies screening and coding procedures to full texts of included articles.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Interpretive systematic review: searches in ERIC and Web of Science (plus Large-scale Assessments in Education journal and IEA Research for Education book series) using keyword combinations around “equity/equality” and education/learning/school/stud* with ILSA datasets (TIMSS, PISA, PIRLS; and ICCS, ICILS). Inclusion criteria: peer-reviewed English-language articles published 1995 onward, empirical studies using TIMSS/PIRLS/PISA/ICCS/ICILS data for compulsory education and making statements about educational quality or equity. Screening proceeded in two stages (title/abstract/conclusion first; then explicit equity/equality in aims/questions), followed by full-text eligibility assessment, resulting in 25 included articles. Only studies using TIMSS, PIRLS, and PISA met the final inclusion criteria; ICCS and ICILS studies were not retained.

data.outcome_summary: This interpretive systematic review synthesizes 25 peer-reviewed articles that conduct secondary analyses using ILSA data to make claims about educational equity. The review does not estimate predictive models or report ML performance metrics; instead, it codes how equity is conceptualized and operationalized across studies and organizes the literature into five equity approaches: ability equity, social equity, ethnic equity, gender equity, and equity of treatment. Across the included studies, equity is frequently operationalized through achievement/ability measures and through relationships between student background and achievement, with social equity being the most prevalent approach. The review also highlights methodological concerns raised in the primary studies, including limitations of cross-sectional designs for causal claims and sampling procedures that may not capture class-level variation. The key implication is that policy interpretations of “equity” from ILSA-based secondary analyses depend strongly on the chosen conceptualization and operationalization, so governments should read these studies with attention to their definitional boundaries.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a systematic review rather than an empirical ML study using ILSA microdata. As a result, there is no student-level analytic sample, no country-level student counts, no PV generation/combining, no missing-data imputation strategy for student records, and no ML algorithms or performance metrics to extract. The “results” are qualitative synthesis outputs (coded equity approaches and patterns) rather than quantitative predictive outcomes.
